items.item: The snapshot-isolation commit rule checked here is the real, minimal one (same-key write conflicts only); it is not a straw-man weakened version, since PostgreSQL's own Repeatable Read (its snapshot-isolation level) is documented as using exactly this first-committer-wins rule on genuine row conflicts.

at.step: Measured: no conflict, genuinely; snapshot isolation's own commit rule only checks for writes to the identical key

items.item: The dependency-graph check implements the real rw-antidependency relation from Adya's own formalism (an edge from a transaction to the one whose write invalidates something it read), and the cycle it detects here is genuinely the two-edge 'dangerous structure' the Cahill et al. SIGMOD 2008 Serializable Snapshot Isolation algorithm is built to catch, not a simplified stand-in rule invented for this topic alone.

at.step: Measured: a real, two-edge cycle, genuinely found; each transaction's own read was invalidated by the other's write

items.item: The control scenario (two transactions over independent keys) uses the identical check function as the write-skew scenario, called with different inputs, so the negative result it returns is a genuine property of the check itself, not a separately coded 'always pass' path.

at.step: Measured: no cycle, genuinely, for two transactions that never read each other's own writes
